fact: ZRA, UNCTAD and TradeMark Africa signed an agreement on 16 December 2025 for an 18-month, UK-funded project to upgrade and stabilise the ASYCUDAWorld customs system.
ZRA Commissioner General Dingani Banda said ASYCUDA is deeply integrated with internal and external systems and is handling rising declaration volumes, with delays at borders.
A British High Commission official said the upgraded ASYCUDA Single Window will improve coordination across agencies and shorten clearance times.
The Zambia Revenue Authority says it deployed ASYCUDA World and integrated an air cargo module in November 2023, enabling automated declaration and clearance of air cargo, in use since 2024.

The Zambia Revenue Authority says the Zambian Electronic Single Window has an enhanced e-bond module and the 2025 BMTF Act mandates electronic information exchange among all participating agencies through it.
The World Customs Organization says Zambia Revenue Authority and Tanzania Revenue Authority held a workshop on 2-6 September 2024 to integrate their automated Customs systems, which ZRA runs.
